newsitem.title: USA: Democrats pull out of U.S. Senate election review.
newsitem.headline: Democrats pull out of U.S. Senate election review.

text.p: Senate Democrats refused to cooperate any longer in a review of a contested Louisiana election and told Republicans Thursday to accept that their man lost to Democrat Mary Landrieu.
"If it goes on ... it is tantamount to a political witch hunt," Democratic Leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota said.
Rules Committee Chairman John Warner, a Virginia Republican, was expected to respond later in the day, an aide said.
"Warner said the investigation continues this morning and investigators are at work," a statement from his office said.
The Republican candidate Louis "Woody" Jenkins has contended that vote fraud allowed Landrieu to claim victory. She won by 5,788 votes out of 1.7 million cast.
Landrieu was sworn into office Jan. 7, pending the outcome of an investigation into Jenkins' complaints.

In making their decision, Democrats said months of work had found little doubt of Landrieu's victory. Senator Wendell Ford of Kentucky, the Democratic leader on the Rules Committee, said the only fraud was "testimony solicited on behalf of Mr. Jenkins by a known criminal."
"There is no way that we, in good conscience, can or should proceed with this investigation," Ford said.
Ford said Democrats had asked the Justice Department to investigate potential witness tampering and interference with the Senate review.
